content.comment_body: Is it possible to use a serial cable for communication between the [product_name] and a PC via the serial COM port, instead of USB? Is this RS232 protocol? Could this setup function?
I’ll proceed with a support request and share any solutions here if available.

Previously, there was a cable for programming older [product_name] versions. The PC side used RS232, but the [product_name] side had a specific [company_name] connector with special signal configuration. More recent USB cables for [product_name] offer the same features, as communication is accomplished through COM ports, and these USB cables include an internal RS232 adapter. Both cable types enable programming of [product_name], but this is only possible with [product_name] software and exclusively for the controller, not for peripherals like displays. Some third-party applications are available online that allow users to monitor [product_name] I/O status without using [product_name] software, providing additional PC interface options. However, I haven’t seen any solution for connecting displays as indicated in your link. Best regards, [user_name]
I was considering whether an RS232 text display (for example, devices similar to OP-3) could retrieve a marker generated by [product_name] through RS232 or a similar approach...

Actually, the first [product_name] version that supports external HMI connections is [version_no], which has a LAN connector. OP3 with RS232 can be used with products like [version_no]. For display connectivity, you’ll need a newer [product_name] version such as [version_no]. These support modern panels or other displays via LAN connectors and are also compatible with devices using S7 or Modbus protocols. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Participants discuss if serial RS232 cabling can connect a [product_name] to a PC or external display. Older [product_name] versions used a proprietary connector on the device side, whereas later models adopted USB with integrated RS232 adapters. Programming is limited to dedicated [product_name] software and is not extended to displays or other peripherals via RS232. Confusion remains about compatibility with certain text displays such as OP-3. Main themes involve hardware interface limitations and dependency on specific software for communication.
analysis.user_expectations: A user anticipates being able to use a standard RS232 cable for direct communication between a [product_name] and a PC or to connect an RS232-compatible text display directly to the [product_name].
